saints.name: St. Andrew Corsini
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A Carmelite friar of Florence who, called from a wayward youth to a life of penance, became a peacemaking bishop of Fiesole…
biography: Born at Florence on 30 November 1302, the feast of St. Andrew, into the noble Corsini family, he spent his youth in dissipation until his mother's rebuke — she had dreamed before his birth of bearing a wolf who became a lamb — turned him to repentance. In 1318 he entered the Carmelites at Santa Maria del Carmine and was ordained in 1328.

Made prior of his convent and known as the Apostle of Florence, he was named bishop of Fiesole by Clement VI in 1349; the reluctant friar hid himself until a vision moved him to accept. As bishop he redoubled his austerities, wearing a hair shirt, and gave himself to the care of the poor.

His noble name won him the hearing of the great and his poverty the love of the humble, so that Urban V sent him as legate to compose the feuds of Bologna; hence he is invoked against civil discord. He died on 6 January 1373, had his cult confirmed by Eugene IV in 1440, and was canonized by Urban VIII in 1629.
saints.knownFor: Reconciling enemies as the peacemaking bishop of Fiesole.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 4 February
